proof:
# Binary joins: unrestricted centers cannot give a uniform stronger constant

This is an exact obstruction to a proposed intermediate strengthening. It is
not a proof or a counterexample to OC. It allows the center anywhere in the
ambient space and uses closed halfspaces throughout.

## 1. Uniform measures on the faces of an affine join

Let r>=2 and D>=1. Let J be an affine simplex with r(D+1) vertices, partitioned
into r disjoint groups of D+1 vertices. Let T_i be the D-simplex spanned by
group i. Give each T_i mass 1/r and uniform intrinsic D-volume. Call the
resulting probability measure nu. Then

    max_y depth_nu(y)=gamma_D/r,
    gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D.                                  (1)

Write the barycentric coordinate functions on J as lambda_ij, and put
tau_i=sum_j lambda_ij. Let g_i be the centroid of T_i and g=r^{-1}sum_i g_i.
For every halfspace containing g, at least one g_i lies in that halfspace:
otherwise its defining affine function would be strictly negative at all
g_i and hence at their average. The ordinary simplex centroid inequality
therefore gives at least gamma_D/r mass in that halfspace. This proves the
lower bound in (1). The simplex centroid inequality here is the ordinary
D-dimensional one; the signed-exponential proof already archived in
candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9 supplies it.

For the upper bound, a point outside J has depth zero by strict separation.
For y in J choose i with t=tau_i(y)>0, and choose j such that

    b=lambda_ij(y)/t >=1/(D+1).

For epsilon>0 put delta=epsilon(1-t)/t and use the closed halfspace whose
affine margin is

    L_epsilon=lambda_ij-b tau_i+delta tau_i-epsilon(1-tau_i).

Its margin at y is zero. On every other component T_k it is the strictly
negative constant -epsilon. On T_i its trace is the simplex cap
lambda_ij>=b-delta. For sufficiently small epsilon this threshold is
positive and at most one; its nu-mass is

    (1/r)(1-b+delta)^D.

Taking epsilon down to zero proves depth_nu(y)<=(1-b)^D/r<=gamma_D/r.
When t=1, delta=0 and the same formula already gives the bound at every
epsilon. The defining normal is nonzero because D>=1 and lambda_ij is
nonconstant on T_i. Importantly, we take an infimum of closed-cap masses;
we do not replace the limiting cap by its open version. At epsilon=0
the other components lie in the boundary and cannot be discarded.

## 2. Realization by a full-dimensional convex body with binary projection

Fix n>=1, put r=2^n, and enumerate the binary vertices z_1,...,z_r so that
the first n+1 are 0,e_1,...,e_n. Put k=r-n-1>=0 and set

    d=k+rD.

Decompose the continuous space as R^k plus r separate copies of R^D.
Set c_i=0 in R^k for i<=n+1, and assign the k standard basis vectors to
the remaining c_i. Let Delta_D=conv(0,e_1,...,e_D) in R^D. At integer
index z_i put the D-simplex

    T_i={c_i} x {0} x ... x Delta_D x ... x {0},

with Delta_D in block i. Let J be the convex hull of these lifted fibers.

The r points (z_i,c_i) are affinely independent in R^{n+k}=R^{r-1}:
differences from the first point have the first n standard coordinates
for the next n points, and the remaining points have distinct standard
coordinates in the final k coordinates. Within every group, its D vertex
differences are the distinct standard vectors in its own continuous block.
Together these are n+k+rD=n+d independent differences. Thus all r(D+1)
vertices of J are affinely independent and J is a full-dimensional compact
simplex, hence a convex body in the required ambient space.

The integer projection of J is [0,1]^n. Its only integer points are its r
binary vertices. Extremality of z_i in that cube forces the z_i-fiber of J
to equal T_i exactly. Consequently J intersect Lambda is precisely the
disjoint union of these T_i. They are isometric D-simplices of positive
finite D-volume; q=D and normalized H_D is exactly nu from section 1.
Therefore (1) is an exact unrestricted-center statement for a genuine
convex-body-induced mixed-integer set.

Here the parameter in OC is the continuous ambient dimension d, rather
than q=D. Since gamma_d<=gamma_D, equation (1) does not contradict OC.

## 3. Full-dimensional positive fibers and weak convergence

For epsilon>0 let

    C_epsilon=J+({0}^n x [-epsilon,epsilon]^d).

This is a convex body with the same integer projection. Its actual integer
fiber at z_i is T_i+[-epsilon,epsilon]^d. In the displayed continuous block
coordinates this is the Cartesian product of

    Delta_D+[-epsilon,epsilon]^D

in block i and intervals of length 2epsilon in all d-D other coordinates,
translated by c_i in the first k coordinates. All r fibers therefore have
the same positive d-volume. In particular the normalized mixed d-volume
nu_epsilon gives mass 1/r to each fiber, and q=d.

Uniform measure on Delta_D+[-epsilon,epsilon]^D converges weakly to uniform
measure on Delta_D. To check this directly, the outer sets decrease to the
compact simplex as epsilon decreases to zero. Their volumes converge to
its positive volume by continuity from above of Lebesgue measure; their
indicator functions converge almost everywhere and are bounded in a fixed
box. The uniform measures on the remaining shrinking intervals converge
to their point masses. Product integration, and then the finite sum over
i, give nu_epsilon weakly convergent to nu. The supports stay in one fixed
compact set and C_epsilon converges to J in Hausdorff distance.

## 4. Upper semicontinuity of the unrestricted maximum depth

We record the limit fact, including boundary mass. Suppose probability
measures mu_l converge weakly to mu, their compact supports lie in a fixed
compact set, and y_l->y. Then

    limsup_l depth_(mu_l)(y_l) <= depth_mu(y).             (2)

It suffices to examine a subsequence realizing the left limsup. For any
fixed nonzero normal a and any eta>0, eventually the through-y_l halfspace
{w:a dot(w-y_l)>=0} is contained in the fixed closed halfspace
H_eta={w:a dot(w-y)>=-eta}. By the closed-set Portmanteau inequality,

    limsup_l depth_(mu_l)(y_l) <= mu(H_eta).

Let eta decrease to zero. Continuity from above gives the mass of the
CLOSED through-y halfspace, including all boundary mass. Taking the infimum
over a proves (2). Through-point halfspaces suffice in the definition,
because any containing halfspace can be translated toward its point until
its boundary contains that point, thereby only decreasing the captured mass.

For each fixed measure, the same argument with the measure constant proves
upper semicontinuity in y. On a compact convex support the maximum is thus
attained. Every point outside that convex support has depth zero. In the
present family, choose maximum-depth points y_epsilon in C_epsilon. Along
any sequence epsilon down to zero, compactness gives a subsequence converging
to a point of J. Applying (2) and (1) yields

    limsup_(epsilon down to 0) max_y depth_(nu_epsilon)(y)
        <= gamma_D/r.                                  (3)

This is an upper bound; no equality in (3) or convergence of maximizers to
a specified point is asserted.

## 5. Exact scope of the obstruction

For fixed n and r=2^n, as the integer D tends to infinity, both gamma_D and
gamma_(rD+r-n-1) tend to 1/e. Hence for every c>1 there is a finite D with

    gamma_D < c gamma_d,       d=rD+r-n-1.

By (3), sufficiently small positive epsilon then gives a full-dimensional
convex body with all integer fibers of positive d-volume for which

    max_(y in ambient space) depth_(nu_epsilon)(y)
        < c 2^(-n) gamma_d.

Thus allowing an unrestricted ambient center does not permit any uniform
multiplicative improvement c>1 over the requested constant, across all
dimensions. This rules out that proposed stronger intermediate objective.
It does not establish nonemptiness of the depth region at the exact OC
level, and it supplies no mixed-integer center with the OC guarantee.
